title: The CRISP Mandate: Architecting a High-Performance VHIE for Vermont's Future
summary: A comprehensive CDO-level technical and fiscal analysis of the strategic necessity to transition management of the Vermont Health Information Exchange (VHIE) from Vermont Information Technology Leaders (VITL) to the CRISP shared services platform to achieve regional interoperability and operational excellence.

children.text: The Strategic Imperative for a New HIE Governance Model

As the Chief Data Officer for the Vermont Agency of Human Services (AHS), I have conducted a rigorous audit of our current health data exchange landscape. The conclusion is undeniable: the legacy architecture managed by Vermont Information Technology Leaders (VITL) has reached its architectural and fiscal ceiling. To meet the mandates of the 2026 Health Innovation Plan, Vermont must pivot toward a collaborative, multi-state shared services model. CRISP (Chesapeake Regional Information System for our Patients) offers the proven, cloud-native infrastructure required to transform the VHIE from a passive repository into a dynamic clinical tool.

CDO Alert: Maintaining the current VITL contract costs the state approximately $2.1M annually in avoidable technical debt and redundant maintenance fees compared to regional shared-service benchmarks.

The current VHIE infrastructure suffers from significant latency in ADT (Admission, Discharge, Transfer) notifications and lacks the native capability to integrate social determinants of health (SDOH) at scale. By moving to the CRISP platform, we gain access to a mature stack that already services Maryland, West Virginia, and the District of Columbia. This transition allows Vermont to benefit from collective R&D, ensuring our clinical community has access to real-time longitudinal patient records without the localized burden of developing every new feature from scratch.
Vermont's patients do not stop needing care at our state borders. Our data infrastructure shouldn't stop there either. The move to CRISP is a move toward a borderless, patient-centric data ecosystem.

children.text: We are proposing an 18-month sunset period for VITL operations. Phase 1 will involve the replication of existing interfaces into the CRISP environment, followed by a Phase 2 validation of clinical data integrity. This visionary shift ensures that Vermont remains a leader in healthcare reform by leveraging economies of scale that a small state simply cannot achieve in isolation. The following audio briefing provides the high-level executive roadmap for this transition.
To further illustrate the success of this model in other jurisdictions, please review the following case study on regional HIE consolidation.

Firing VITL is not a decision based on past failures, but on future requirements. By migrating the VHIE to CRISP, we are securing a scalable, innovative, and fiscally responsible future for Vermont's healthcare providers and citizens alike. The transition protocol is ready for immediate execution.
